la:verb:pecco.gloss: to sin, transgress, commit a wrongdoing
senses: to sin, transgress, commit a wrongdoing
la:verb:pecco.html:
pecco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[often referred to Sanscr. pāpa, pāpaka, wicked; but better to root pik-, to be angry; cf.: piget, pigeo, and Fick, Vergl. Wört. 632], to miss or mistake any thing; to do amiss, to transgress, to commit a fault, to offend, sin: peccare est tamquam transilire lineas,: alius magis alio vel peccat vel recte facit,; : peccare largiter,to make a great mistake,; .—With acc.: si unam peccavisses syllabam,: aliquid, to offend in any respect: plura in aliquā re,: Empedocles multa alia peccat,: eadem fere,: talia peccandi jam mihi finis erit,.—With in and acc.: si quid in te peccavi . . . in me ipsum peccavi vehementius,: in rem publicam, (al. in re publicā).—With erga aliquem, .—In aliquo or in aliquā re: quod in eo (Valerio) peccandi Germanis causa non esset,: in servo necando semel peccatur,: in hoc eodem peccat Hieronymus,: non modo in vitā sed saepissime et in poëmatis et in oratione peccatur,.—With abl. alone: et pecuniā et mollibus consultis,: libidine,.—With dat. of person (late Lat.): Domino,; .—De aliquă re, Caecil. ap. .—
In partic., of sexual sin: quid inter-Est in matronā, ancillā, peccesve togatā?; ; .—
Transf., of animals and inanim. things, to fail, miscarry: ne Peccet (equus) ad extremum ridendus,: unus de toto peccaverat orbe comarum Anulus,: si senseris vina peccatura,.—Hence, peccans, antis, P. a., sinful, full of sin: unus dies bene actus peccanti immortalitati anteponendus,.— Comp.: peccantius,more faulty, worse,.—
As subst.: peccans, antis, comm., an offender, sinner: non prodest latere peccantibus. : peccantium poena,: ad officium peccantes redire cogeret,.—Adv.: peccanter, wrongly, incorrectly, falsely, : definire aliquid,.
la:verb:pecco.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:noun:pecunia.html:
pĕcūnĭa, ae (on the oldest inscrr., also written PEQVNIA, as PEQVDES, PEQVLIVM), f.
pecus, because the wealth of the ancients consisted in cattle: pecus, a quo pecunia universa, quod in pecore pecunia tum consistebat pastoribus, Müll.; cf. Fest. s. v. peculatus, p. 212 and 213 Müll.
,
property, riches, wealth (cf.: divitiae, res, bona, etc.).
In gen.: pecunia sacrificium fieri dicebatur, cum frugum fructuumque causā mola pura offerebatur in sacrificio, quia omnis res familiaris, quam nunc pecuniam dicimus, ex his rebus constaret, and 245 Müll.: SI FVRIOSVS EST AGNATORVM GENTILIVMQVE IN EO PECVNIAQVE EIVS POTESTAS ESTO, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. ; ib. ap. Ulp. Fragm. tit. 11, § 14: QVI CORONAM PARIT IPSE PECVNIAVE EIVS VIRTVTIS ERGO DVITOR EI, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. : pecuniam facere,to accumulate property,: in alienam pecuniam invadere,: ut pecunia fortunisque nostris contentus sit,: familiae aliquot cum mapalibus pecoribusque suis (ea pecunia illis est), etc.,.—
In partic., money (syn.: argentum, nummus): qui dabant olim pecuniam, non adnumerabant eam, sed appendebant,: praesenti pecuniā mercari aliquid,: omnia vaenibunt praesenti pecuniā,: pecunia numerata,: pecunia publica ex aerario erogata,: certa,a specified sum,: potestas pecuniae conficiendae,: permagnam ex illā re pecuniam confici posse,: pecuniam cogere a civitatibus,, § 171: pecuniam numerare alicui ab aerario,, § 177: pecuniam publicam domum suam convertere,, § 176: pecunias civitatibus distribuere ... avertere atque auferre,, § 171: devorare pecuniam publicam,, § 177: pecuniam alicui dissolvere,, § 180: solvere alicui,: pecunias conferre ad statuas,: alicui conferre in usum ejus, id. Fl. 23, 55: transferre in quaestum et fenerationem,: deferre alicui,: credita nobis,: gravi fenore occupare,: collocatam habere,: ex aerario exhaurire, ex vectigalibus redigere,: exige pecuniam a civitatibus,: ab sociis maximam pecuniam auferre,, § 224: plura mala nobis exhibet quam aliud quidquam,: majore tormento possidetur quam quaeritur,: et pecuniae obediunt omnia,.—So in plur.: pecunias exigere, capere, imperare,: pecunias auferre ab aliquo,: pecunias sumere mutuas,, § 28; 2, 2, 70, § 170: mutuas pecunias faenore quaerens,; ; cf. Zumpt ad : DIES PECVNIAE,the day of payment,.—Hence,
(Late Lat.) Copper coins: scenicis numquam aurum, numquam argentum, vix pecuniam donavit,.—
Personified: Pecunia,the goddess of gain,; cf. .—Also, an epithet of Jupiter, , 7, 11; cf. ; cf. also .

senses: heart, breast, as the seat of emotion
person, individual (as a being of passion)
la:noun:pectus.html:
pectus, ŏris, n.
kindred with the Sanscr. vakshas, pectus
,
the breast, in men and animals.
Lit., the breast, the breastbone: pectus, hoc est ossa praecordiis et vitalibus natura circumdedit,; cf. ; : meum cor coepit in pectus emicare,: dignitas, quae est in latitudine pectoris,: summis digitis pectus appetere,; : pectore adverso,: aequo pectore,upright, not inclined to one side,: pectore in adverso ensem Condidit,: in pectusque cadit pronus,: latum demisit pectore clavum,; et saep.; .—In the poets freq., in plur., of a person's breast: hasta volans perrumpit pectora ferro, Liv. Andron. ap. P.; .—
Transf.
The stomach (poet.): reserato pectore diras Egerere inde dapes ... gestit,.—
The breast.
As the seat of affection, courage, etc., the heart, feelings, disposition: somnum socordiamque ex pectore oculisque amovere,: Ah, guttula Pectus ardens mi adspersisti,i. e. a little comforted,: in amicitiā, nisi, ut dicitur, apertum pectus videas, etc.,: si non ipse amicus per se amatur toto pectore ut dicitur,: pietate omnium pectora imbuere,: metus insidens pectoribus,; : quinam pectora semper impavida repens terror invaserit,: in eodem pectore nullum est honestorum turpiumque consortium,; : te vero ... jam pectore toto Accipio,: his ubi laeta deae permulsit pectora dictis,: robur et aes triplex circa pectus erat,; : pectoribus mores tot sunt quot in orbe figurae,: mollities pectoris,tender-heartedness,; ; so, pectus amicitiae,a friendly heart, a friend,; ; .— Of courage, bravery: cum tales animos juvenum et tam certa tulistis Pectora,: te vel per Alpium juga ... Forti sequemur pectore,; .—Of conscience: vita et pectore puro,: pectora casta,.—
The soul, spirit, mind, understanding: de hortis toto pectore cogitemus,; so, incumbe toto pectore ad laudem,: onerandum complendumque pectus maximarum rerum et plurimarum suavitate,: quod verbum in pectus Jugurthae altius descendit,; : (stultitiam tuam) in latebras abscondas pectore penitissumo,: multipotens pectus habere, ut copias ... pectore promat suo, Fleck.: haben' tu amicum quoi pectus sapiat? id. Trin. 1, 2, 53; : at Cytherea novas artes, nova pectore versat Consilia,: oculis pectoris aliquid haurire,; : memori referas mihi pectore cuncta,: nunc adbibe puro Pectore verba,; : pectore arripere artes,: pectus est quod disertos facit, et vis mentis,; : succinctaque pectora curis,: rara occulti pectoris vox,i. e. a reserved disposition,: dicere de summo pectore,i.e. without much reflection,.—Of inspired persons: incaluitque deo quem clausum pectore habebat,; ; .—
The person, individual, regarded as a being of feeling or passion: cara sororum Pectora,: mihi Thesea pectora juncta fide,: pectus consulis gerere,; cf. ; ; .

la:noun:peccatum.html:
peccātum, i, n.
pecco
,
a fault, error, mistake, transgression, sin (syn.: delictum, culpa): pro peccatis supplicium sufferre,: corrigere,: peccata remordent,: recte facta sola in bonis actionibus ponens, prave, id est peccata, in malis,: ut peccatum est, patriam prodere, parentes violare, fana depeculari, quae sunt in effectu; sic timere, sic maerere, sic in libidine esse, peccatum est, etiam sine effectu,: culpa ac peccatum,: multitudo vitiorum peccatorumque,; : quo illi crimine peccatoque perierunt?: libidinum peccatorumque licentia,: confiteri,; : paucis verbis tria magna peccata,blunders,: in peccata incidere,: luere peccata,: peccati conscius,: peccatis poenas aequas irrogare,: peccatis veniam commodare, Tac Agr. 19: abstinere peccatis,. Here, too, doubtless belongs: nam eā aetate jam sum, ut non siet peccato mi ignosci aequom .—
Transf. (eccl. Lat.).
Guilt: si non venissem peccatum non haberent,: cognatio pec-cati,; .—
The punishment of sin: peccatum vestrum apprehendet vos,: ipse peccata multorum tulit,.

la:noun:pecus.gloss: A group of large domestic animals: a herd of cattle, horses, or donkeys; such animals in a collective sense: cattle and equines.
senses: A group of large domestic animals: a herd of cattle, horses, or donkeys; such animals in a collective sense: cattle and equines.
Any other group of animals, imagined as a herd or flock; such animals collectively: beasts.
A mindless group of people: "cattle", "sheep", rabble, the mob.
Any individual animal, conceived as a member or usual member of a flock or herd.
la:noun:pecus.html:
pĕcus, pecŏris, n.
Zend, pacu, cattle; cf. Goth. faihu; Angl.-Sax. feó, cattle; Germ. Vieh; Engl. fee. Fick refers the word to root pag- of pango, etc.
,
cattle, as a collective, a herd (opp.: pecus, pecudis, a single head of cattle).
Lit.
In gen.: bubulum pecus,horned cattle,; : ovile,sheep, prooem.: caprile,: pecus majus et minus ... de pecore majore, in quo sunt ad tres species naturā discreti, boves, asini, equi,: equinum,a stud,: setigerum pecus, the bristly herd, i. e. the herd of swine, : flammatum pecus,the thirsty steeds,: volatile pecus,fowls, hens,: ignavum fucos pecus a praesepibus arcent,i. e. the drones,.—So of bees, .—Of seals: omne cum Proteus pecus egit altos Visere montes,; cf. of fish: aquatile,.—
In partic, of sheep, small cattle, a flock: pecori et bubus diligenter substernatur. Scabiem pecori et jumentis caveto (shortly after: frondem substernito ovibus bubusque),: boni pastoris est pecus tondere non deglubere, Tiber. ap. : balatus pecorum,; .—
Transf.
Of a single animal: inque pecus magnae subito vertare parentis = pecudem,the young lion,; Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 6, 7, 9.—In late and eccl. lat. the distinction

between pecus, f., and pecus, n., nearly disappears, and the latter is found in all senses of the words; cf. ; ; .—

Contemptuously, or as a term of abuse, of persons, cattle: mutum et turpe pecus,: o imitatores, servum pecus,: simul ite, Dindymenae dominae vaga pecora,: sed venale pecus Corythae posteritas,.

la:noun:pecus#2.gloss: A single herd animal, especially a head of cattle, a horse.
senses: A single herd animal, especially a head of cattle, a horse.
A single animal, a beast, especially smaller livestock or livestock taken generally.
A mindless or violent person: a brute, an animal.

la:noun:pecu.html:
pĕcu (dat. pecui, Lucil. ap. Gell. infra; plur.: pecua, pecuda;
gen. pecuum, Cato ap. : pecubus,), n.
v. pecus
, cattle, esp. the larger kinds (mostly ante-class.): pastor harum dormit, quom eunt sic a pecu palitantes,the flock,: ne balant quidem, quom a pecu cetero apsunt,: luna muribus fibras Et pecui addit, Lucil. ap. .—In plur.: pastores pecuaque salva servassis, an old formula of prayer in : homines, pecua beluasque, Naev. ap. ; so ; ; : (asinus) non generatur in Ponto, nec aequinoctio verno, ut cetera pecua admittitur,: pecua ruri pascere,.—
Transf.
Plur.: pecua, the places where cattle are kept, pastures, etc.: cum hostium copiae non longe absunt, pecua relinquuntur, agri cultura deseritur, Halm ad loc.: Italia contremuit, statim pecua agrique deserta,.—
Money (cf. pecunia): pecua in cruminā defero,: pecuum, Cato ap. Paul. ex Müll.: greges pecuum, Host. ap. P.—
Pecu squamosum, i. e. fish, (but in , the correct read. is pigris balantibus; v. Lachm. ad h. l.).

senses: the reed or sley of a weaver's loom
an instrument with which the strings of the lyre are struck; a plectrum, quill
la:noun:pecten.html:
pecten, ĭnis, m.
pecto
,
a comb.
Prop., for the hair, ; : deducit pectine crines,; ; ; .—
Transf., of things resembling a comb.
The reed or sley of a weaver's loom: arguto tenues percurrens pectine telas,; ; cf. ; .—
The weaver's art, weaving: victa est Pectine Niliaco jam Babylonis acus,.—
An instrument for heckling flax or combing wool, a comb, card, heckle, ; ; .—
A rake: tonsam raro pectine verrit humum,; ; .—
A clasping of the hands in distress, .—Of the mingling of the oars of two vessels: mixtis obliquo pectine remis, dub. (al. pectore).—
Pecten dentium, a row of teeth, Prud. στεφ. 10, 934.—
A stripe or vein in wood, .—
The hair of the pubes, ; .—Also, the sharebone, .—
A kind of dance: Amazonius,.—
An instrument with which the strings of the lyre were struck: jamque eadem digitis, jam pectine pulsat eburno, Serv.; .—
Transf.
A lyre, .—
A poem or song: dum canimus sacras alterno pectine Nonas,i. e. in distichs,.—
A kind of shell-fish, a scallop: pectinibus patulis jactat se molle Tarentum,; ; ; ; 11, 51, 112, § 267; 32, 11, 53, § 150.—
Pecten Veneris, a plant, perh. Venus's comb, needle-weed, .

senses: to give someone a thrashing, thrash
la:verb:pecto.html:
pecto, pexi (pexui, ), pexum and pectĭtum, 3, v. a.
Gr. πέκω, πεκτέω, to comb, shear; πόκος, fleece; Lat. pecten
,
to comb.
Lit.: tenues comas,: longas comas,: caesariem,: capillos,; cf.: pexisti capillum, Maec. ap. P: barbam,: pectebat ferum (cervum),: capilli pexi,: pexa barba,: ille pexus pinguisque doctor,.—In a Greek construction: ipsa comas pectar,.—
Transf.
To comb, card, heckle: stuppa pectitur ferreis hamis,: pectitae lanae,.—
To dress, hoe, weed, : pectita tellus,.—Hence,
Trop., comic.: aliquem fusti or pugnis, to give one a dressing or thrashing: leno pugnis pectitur,: pugnis,: aliquem fusti,.—Hence, pexus (as a surname, written PEXSVS, PEXSA, ; Marin. Iscriz. Alb. p. 91), a, um, P. a., woolly, that still has the nap on, new: tunica,: vestes,.—Hence: pexa munera, prob. a new woolly toga, .—
Transf.: folium,woolly,.

la:verb:peccatus.html:
peccātus, ūs, m.
id.
,
a failing, fault, trespass (very rare): in manifesto peccatu teneri,, acc. to (al. peccato).

la:adj:pecuniarius.html:
pĕcūnĭārĭus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
of or belonging to money, pecuniary (class.): rei pecuniariae socius,in a money matter,: res,: praemia rei pecuniariae magna,great rewards in money,; : lis,: quaestiones,: poena,: condemnatio,to pay a fine,.—
Subst.: pĕcūnĭārĭus, χρηματιστής, Gloss. Gr. Lat.—Adv.: pĕcūnĭārĭē, pecuniarily: i. q. pecuniariter. .

la:adj:pecuniosus.html:
pĕcūnĭōsus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
that has much money, moneyed, rich, wealthy.
Lit. (class.): tum erat res in pecore et locorum possessionibus, ex quo pecuniosi et locupletes vocabantur,: homines copiis rei familiaris locupletes et pecuniosi,: feminae pecuniosiores,: homo pecuniosissimus,; . —
Transf., that brings money, gain ful: artes,.

peccātrix, īcis, f.
id.
,
a female sinner (post-class.), ; Hier. adv. Joann. Jerosol. n. 4; .—
Adj., sinning, sinful: peccatrix anima, prooem. 35: gens,: generatio,: radix,.

la:adj:pecuarius.html:
pĕcŭārĭus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
of or belonging to cattle: res pecuaria,: pecuarii greges,herds of cattle,: quaestio,: negotiatio,: canis,: res,a stock of cattle, live stock,.—
Subst.
pĕcŭārĭus, ii, m.
A cattle-breeder, grazier, : diligentissimus agricola et pecuarius,.—
A farmer of the public pastures: damnatis aliquot pecuariis,; Inscr. Don. cl. 9, n. 13.—
pĕcŭārĭa, ae, f., a stock of cattle: omnis pecuariae pecus fundamentum,: ipse pecuarias habui grandes, in Apuliā oviarias, in Reatino equarias,, praef. § 6; 2, 1, 3.—Also, cattle-breeding: librum de pecuariā,—
pĕcŭārĭa, ōrum, n., herds of cattle: mitte in Venerem pecuaria primus,; ; .

la:noun:peculatus.gloss: embezzlement of public money or property, peculation
senses: embezzlement of public money or property, peculation
la:noun:peculatus.html:
pĕcūlātus (PEQVLATVS, Lex Apparit.,
v.in the foll.), ūs, m.
peculor
.
Lit., an embezzlement of public money, peculation: peculatus furtum publicum a pecore dictum, sicut et pecunia, eo quod antiqui Romani nihil praeter pecora habebant, Müll.: perfidia et peculatus ex urbe si exulant,; : peculatum facere,: accusari peculatus,: peculatus damnari,; : SINE MALO PEQVLATV, Lex Apparit. Grut. 628: judices qui peculatu provincias quassavissent, Cod. Th. 9, 28, 1: ad legem Juliam peculatus,.—
Transf., of the caprice of love: perfidiosus est Amor. Si. Ergo in me peculatum facit, .

senses: to defraud the public; to embezzle public funds

pĕcūlor, āri,
v. dep. n. [peculium], to defraud the public, to embezzle the public money, to peculate: rem publicam,.—Hence, pĕcūlans, antis, P. a.—As subst. plur.: pĕcūlantĭa, ium, n., peculations: vestra,.

peculor

la:noun:peculium.gloss: private property (originally in the form of cattle, but later in the form of savings)
senses: private property (originally in the form of cattle, but later in the form of savings)
la:noun:peculium.html:
pĕcūlĭum, ii, n.
pecus
, lit.,
property in cattle; hence, as in early times all property consisted of cattle, in gen., property.
Lit.
In gen.: peculi sui prodigi (servi),: cupiditas peculii,: cura peculi, Serv.; .—
In partic., private property.
What the master of the house saves and lays by, money laid by, savings, .—
What a wife owns as her independent property, and over which her husband has no control, a private purse, paraphernalia, .—
That which is given by a father or master to his son, daughter, or slave, as his or her private property: frugi sum, nec potest peculium enumerari,: adimere servis peculium,; : filii,; cf. : Juliam uxorem peculio concesso a patre praebitisque annuis, fraudavit,: cultis augere peculia servis,fees,.—
Castrense, the private property of a son acquired by military service, with the consent of his father (profecticium), or by inheritance through his mother (adventicium); then called quasi castrense, sqq.; ; cf. .—
= membrum virile, ; ; ; ; cf. peculiatus.—
Trop., that which belongs to one's self, one's own.—Of a letter: sine ullo ad me peculio veniet?without any thing for myself,.—Of the people of lsrael: erunt mihi, in die quā ego facio, in peculium,.

la:adj:peculiaris.html:
pĕcūlĭāris, e, adj.
peculium
,
of or relating to private property.
Lit.: peculiaris causa,concerning property,: peculiari nomine,on account of property,.—
Transf.
One's own, belonging to one (cf. proprius): etiam opilio, qui pascit alienas oves, aliquam habet peculiarem,: ovem tibi dabo peculiarem,: ut peculiare aliquid in fundo pascere liceat,: aedes,; : nummi,: vinum,: vectigalibus peculiares servos praeposuit,belonging to him, his own,: prolatos manu sua e peculiaribus loculis suis .—
One's own, belonging particularly to one's self, not held in common with others; proper, special, peculiar: venio ad Lysaniam, peculiarem tuum, Deciane, testem,: hoc mihi peculiare fuerit,: edictum,; : quasi proprio suo et peculiari deo,: Africae peculiare, quod in oleastro inserit,: haec sunt peculiaria Arabiae,; : me peculiaris quidem impedit ratio,; : luce peculiari nitere,: ut sis ei populus peculiaris,: in populum peculiarem,.—
Singular, particular, extraordinary, peculiar (post-Aug.): peculiari merito,: peculiare munus,.—Adv.: pĕcūlĭārĭ-ter.
As private property: quaedam etiam ignorantes possidemus, id est quae servi peculiariter paraverunt,; .—
Especially, particularly, peculiarly: folia peculiariter cruribus vitiosis utilia,: medicinae peculiariter curiosus,; ; ; (but in , the correct read. is peculiaris, not peculiarius; v Sillig ad h. l.).
